response.sql: SELECT customer_id, COUNT(*) AS order_count, CAST(COUNT(*) AS REAL) / (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM Orders) AS share FROM Orders GROUP BY customer_id ORDER BY share DESC, customer_id ASC LIMIT 10

assumptions.assumption: Share is the customer's order count divided by the total number of rows in Orders, computed as a floating-point (non-integer) division and not rounded.

Only customers with at least one order appear, since the ranking is by order share. Ties are broken by customer_id ascending so the top 10 is deterministic. Share can never be NULL here because customer_id is NOT NULL, so the 'missing values last' instruction has no effect.
